messages:
emily: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small infra piece I call 'resilience-bridge' that centralizes canary signal fusion and emits graded degrade/fallback intents to the router. Primary goal: reduce duplicated logic across platform, make automatic fallback decisions auditable.
raj: Can you sketch the high-level flow? Is this inline in the router or a separate control plane service?
emily: Separate control plane service. Router subscribes to decisions via gRPC stream. Benefits: single place for signal aggregation (latency, error-rate, perf regressions, quality evals).
mason: Concern: adding another hop for decisioning could add 1-3ms. For latency-sensitive paths that matters. How do we keep fast-fail local?
emily: Agree. Plan is hybrid: router has a local fast-path for simple heuristics + default TTL for decisions. Resilience-bridge handles complex fusion and issues longer lived policies that the router caches.
olivia: How do we avoid cache drift: suppose a canary degrades but bridge is slow to propagate rollback intent — clients keep hitting bad model for a few mins.
emily: Two mitigations: 1) short-term emergency signals via router-local circuit-tripper when spike > X; 2) versioned policies with monotonic IDs so routers can detect stale policy and re-request.
raj: What are the primary signals? Latency p95, token error spikes, quality eval fail rate, and explicit rollback requests from release pipeline. Do we weight them?
mason: We should. Example: quality drift should outweigh a transient latency blip. Need pluggable weight config per tenant.
emily: Exactly — policy has signal weights and thresholds. Example proto: ```
message DecisionPolicy {
  string id = 1;
  repeated SignalWeight signals = 2;
  int32 min_observation_window_ms = 3;
  int32 fallback_ttl_sec = 4;
}
```
olivia: Observability: decisions must link to the input signals (trace ids) so SRE can audit. Also store a compact diff of model outputs for quality signals (hash+sample).
mason: +1 on trace ids. Also we need a 'dry-run' mode where bridge emits intents but router doesn't act — used for validating policy before enforcement.
emily: We'll add a subscribe mode: enforcement = [off|dry-run|on]. Bridge must export metrics: decisions_emitted, decisions_applied (router ack), decision_latency_ms.
deploy-bot: [canary-status] Canary 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z model-text-v2 -> 7.8% error spike at 09:10, latency p95 +24%
raj: One tradeoff: centralizing increases blast radius if bridge bugs. Do we gate by per-cluster scoping and rate-limit impacts?
emily: Yes — policies are scoped by tenant/region and we plan a hierarchical fail-open default: if bridge unreachable, routers use last-known cached safe policy or fall back to global conservative policy.
olivia: What's the rollout plan for bridge itself? We must canary the canary controller. :)
emily: Start with opt-in tenants, run bridge in passive dry-run for 2 weeks, then enable enforcement for low-traffic tenants followed by a staggered ramp. Also add manual override in Console.
mason: Action items: 1) emily to draft API proto + cache TTL semantics; 2) raj to sketch router fast-path heuristics; 3) olivia to write observability+audit requirements.
emily: I'll put a PR with proto + simple simulator. thanks all. :thumbsup:
